records.name: Menschwork
records.summary: A nonprofit for Jewish men of all ages. It runs online support groups, workshops, and Mussar study, plus a yearly retreat where men build friendship and meaning together.
records.what_you_do: Join an online MenschGroup for confidential peer support, or sign up for the yearly men's retreat in Falls Village, Connecticut.

schedule.text: Online MenschGroups meet about twice a month for 90 minutes, at a time set by each group. The Jewish Men's Retreat is held once a year.

cost.text: MenschGroups cost $150 for a six-month period, and limited financial help is available through a confidential request form. The yearly retreat asks for a $250 deposit, and first-time attendees get $50 off.

first_step.how: Register for a MenschGroup on the Register for a Program page, or email menschgroups@menschwork.org with questions first.
first_step.basis: Joining a MenschGroup costs $150 for six months before you meet the group, and the retreat asks for a deposit, so a paid step comes first.
first_step.what_to_expect: A MenschGroup is a confidential online group for personal sharing that meets about twice a month for 90 minutes. Members listen without giving advice or feedback, and the facilitator may open with a prompt tied to the weekly Torah portion. The retreat in Falls Village, Connecticut starts around 4:30 pm on a Friday and ends by 2 pm on Sunday, with prayer services and small groups of 5 to 8 men that meet three times.
first_visit_tips: The Fall 2026 MenschGroup period runs July 1 to December 31, 2026, and the site says new groups are forming now.
Retreat roommates are assigned unless you name one, and a single room costs extra only when one is open.
Wassaic station on the Metro-North Harlem line is about a 30 minute taxi ride from the retreat center.
The fellowship for men aged 18 to 35 attending their first or second retreat has its own application page.

records.notes: The Sept 1 payment deadline from tier 1 is dropped because it has passed and the retreat pages do not repeat it. Whether non-Jewish men may join the MenschGroups or the retreat is not stated. Men of Mishkan, co-host of the 2024 Philadelphia Mensch Day, is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Mid Atlantic Social Club
records.summary: A club for men and fathers that supports its own members, mentors young people, and runs community drives for food, back-to-school supplies, and coats.
records.what_you_do: Join the youth group as a mentor, help with community engagement, or come to the club's community days and fundraisers.

schedule.text: Full members get monthly social events, quarterly round tables, and monthly community giveback volunteer events. Meeting times are not listed on the site.

cost.text: The site does not list membership dues. Gala tickets for the November fundraiser are sold online, and the price is not shown.

first_step.how: Fill in the membership application on the Membership page, then wait for the club to be in touch.
first_step.basis: Community days are open to the public and the club has a clear membership form, but the club contacts you after you apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical meeting or volunteer shift. Full members get monthly social events, quarterly round tables, and monthly community giveback events, and the community days hand out school supplies, food, and clothes with games and raffles. The site does not say how long these run or who usually attends.
first_visit_tips: Check the Events page for an RSVP link before a community day, since the site shows an RSVP button for them.
The site does not list meeting times, so ask the club for the youth group schedule before you apply.

records.notes: Tier 1 gave a josh@ address for the youth group, but no such address appears on the pages read, so the contact here is the info@ address shown on the contact page. The membership page shows staff addresses that differ from info@, and the footer contains a template placeholder address, so check before sharing any address. Facebook and Instagram links are kept from tier 1.

records.name: Mt. Airy Airmen
records.summary: A youth basketball organization offering skill training, team training, competitive leagues and tournaments, and an AAU travel basketball program. Players enroll through the website's contact form.
records.what_you_do: Youth athletes train with the team, play in leagues and tournaments, or join the AAU travel program. The site lists six coaches by first name.

schedule.text: Practice days, times, and game dates are not listed on the site.

cost.text: Fees and fee assistance are not listed on the site. A sponsor and donations page exists, with no amounts shown.

first_step.how: Fill in the contact form on the website with your name, email, and phone, and ask about enrolling.
first_step.basis: Enrollment runs through a contact form, and the site does not say whether there are tryouts or how players are placed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say what a first practice looks like, how long it runs, or where it meets. Enrollment starts with the contact form. Ask about tryouts, placement, practice times, and fees before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Ask where practices are held and how often they meet, since the site does not say.
Ask about fees and fee help, since none are listed.

records.notes: Status changed from probably_active to dormant. The newest dated item on the site is a July 2023 testimonial on the services page, which is more than 24 months old, and the blog has no dates. The site still loads and takes enrollment by form, so the owner may want to review this status. One web search found no news about the group. Age groups, practice places, and fees are not published.

records.name: Northeast Feltmakers Guild
records.summary: A volunteer-run guild for people who make felt, at every skill level. It holds meetings and workshops on Zoom, and members get a learning library, in-person workshops, and a yearly retreat.
records.what_you_do: Become a member for $50 a year to get meetings, online programs, subsidized workshops, and retreat access, or volunteer on one of the guild's committees.

schedule.text: Regular meetings and workshops run on Zoom, with days and times not shown on the pages read. Members also get a yearly spring retreat and a yearly November guild meeting.

cost.text: Membership is $50 a year and renews automatically unless you cancel first. Members get free access to meetings and online programs, subsidized workshops, scholarship opportunities for some events, and access to retreats.

first_step.how: Click Join on the Join Us page to become a member for $50 a year, then sign up for the next Zoom meeting or workshop.
first_step.basis: The homepage says all skill levels are welcome and the Join button is clear, but the join page lists free meeting access as a member perk, so a first look may need the $50 membership.
first_step.what_to_expect: Regular meetings and workshops run on Zoom, and members can take in-person workshops that the guild arranges during the year. Several in-person events named on the site are in other states, so check each event's location before you plan to attend. The site does not say how long a meeting runs or who usually attends.
first_visit_tips: Ask on the contact form whether non-members can join the Zoom meetings before you pay the $50.
Membership renews each year on its own, so cancel before the renewal date if you do not want to keep it.
Check the Upcoming Events page for registration links before each meeting.

records.notes: Tier 1 said meetings are open to everyone and the tutorial library is free. The join page says members get free meeting access, and the Learning Library sits under the Members' Area menu. Public access to meetings was not confirmed, so this record does not promise a free first visit. The Philadelphia address is the IRS mailing address, and the in-person workshops named on the site have been held in Lancaster PA, Peterborough NH, West Danville VT and Worcester MA, so the owner may want to decide whether this counts as serving Philadelphia. The recorded programs page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Event dates on the site have weekdays but no year, so they are not used. The contact page shows two addresses, and the one from tier 1 is kept.

records.name: PMW International Educational Rescue Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that raises money so children and youth can pay for school costs such as tuition, uniforms, and books. The one program its site describes is school technology in Jamaica.
records.what_you_do: Donate to the foundation's education fund, or ask by phone or through the contact form whether a volunteer or student role is open. The site does not describe volunteer roles.

cost.text: No fee is described on the site. The donation page suggests $10, $50, or $100, and says gifts go to students' school costs such as tuition, uniforms, and books.

first_step.how: Use the Get in touch form on pmwrescue.org, or call 215-760-6190, to ask how to help a student or volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site does not describe a volunteer role, a program session, or a way to join, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit, a volunteer shift, or a program session. Its one named office address is a P.O. Box, so a first step is a phone call or a message through the contact form.
first_visit_tips: Ask which programs take volunteers in Philadelphia, since the one program the site describes is in Jamaica.
Ask how a donation reaches a student, since the site does not explain how funds are allocated.

records.notes: Verdict question for owner: the only program the site describes is in Jamaica, and no Philadelphia program or volunteer route appears on the pages read, so out_of_area is possible. Kept as publish from tier 1 for now. The displayed email is sharon@pmwrescue.org, but the link behind it points to a placeholder address (info@mysite.com), so check before relying on it. The only year on the site is in a footer copyright, which is not evidence. Tutoring is the closest interest tag; the site describes school cost support, not tutoring.

records.name: Philly Truce Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs Peace Patrol, a neighborhood safety team that hires men who were involved in the justice system, including people coming home from prison. It also holds a community parade and games.
records.what_you_do: Fill in a volunteer form on the site, or apply through the PEACE PATROL form for a patrol job. Volunteers help make neighborhoods safer and support people coming home from prison.

schedule.text: Peace Patrol works in short hourly patrols of no more than 30 minutes, from set meeting points on regular routes. Shift times are not published on the pages read.

cost.text: Volunteering has no fee, and the site invites donations.

first_step.how: Fill out the general volunteer form linked on phillytruce.com, or the separate PEACE PATROL form if you want patrol work.
first_step.basis: Public volunteer and PEACE PATROL forms are linked from the site, though the pages do not say what training, gear, or pay a patrol involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: Patrols run in short, hourly stretches of no more than 30 minutes, starting from set meeting points on regular routes. Teams include justice-impacted men, and the site also names community members and police personnel as participants. The site does not say what gear, training, or pay is provided, so ask before a first shift.
first_visit_tips: Call 267-458-7823 to ask what a patrol shift involves, since the site does not explain it.
Use the PEACE PATROL form for patrol work, and the general volunteer form for other help.

records.notes: The patrol calendar page loaded with no listings, so no shift times are published. The newest dated item is the July 4, 2025 parade and games. The 2025 patrol figures have no month, and copyright years are not evidence. The history page dates the program start to 2021. The community tags come from the mission statement on the homepage.

records.name: Poreuomai
records.summary: A faith-based missions group that sends people on short and long mission trips, offers a missions internship, and runs an academy with a course catalog. The trips listed on the site go to Jamaica and Tobago.
records.what_you_do: Join a short-term or long-term mission trip, apply for a missions internship, take a course, or sign up to volunteer.

schedule.text: Mission trips are scheduled trip by trip, with dates posted on the short-term trips page. The site lists no regular meeting times.

locations.label: Office (per website)
locations.address: P.O. Box 37, Highgate, St. Mary, Jamaica

cost.text: Trip and internship costs are not stated on the site. The course Demystifying Discipleship costs $59 as a one-time payment.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer sign-up form on poreuomai.org and wait for the group to contact you, or call (301) 518-3856.
first_step.basis: The volunteer and internship routes both start with a form and a review or contact step, and the site does not say what the work involves or who can apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical volunteer shift or how long one lasts. Hands-on work is described as serving churches, schools, and communities, and the listed trips go to partner churches in Jamaica and Tobago. The group contacts you after you send the form.
first_visit_tips: Ask about cost, trip length, and who can go before you apply, since the site does not list them.
The site also lists a WhatsApp number, (876) 471-1808, for questions.

records.notes: Status is active because the newest dated item is a newsletter issue dated March 2026. The trips page lists a Tobago trip for August 2026 and a Jamaica trip for July 2027, but the Tobago sign-up link points to a Jamaica page and the Jamaica link carries a 2025 slug, so the trips list may be out of date. The Exponential Conference (March 2026) has no sign-up link. The site names no denomination, so faith is left out. Verdict question for owner: the trips go to Jamaica and Tobago, and the Philadelphia office is the only local address. The volunteer page says service is local or global, so this is kept as publish.
